title: Shang and Zhou China: Oracle Bones and the Mandate of Heaven

cards.h: Fortune-telling is where Chinese writing began
cards.b:
Imagine a king who wants to ask the gods, 'Will it rain? Will my toothache end? Should I attack?' He gives a priest a turtle shell and a hot poker.

The cracks answer. And the question is scratched into the shell. That is the oldest Chinese writing we have.

The Shang ruled the Yellow River region from about 1600 to 1046 BCE (dates are approximate). Their late capital was Anyang, where archaeologists dug up palaces, tombs, and horse chariots.

They made superb bronze ritual vessels, huge and decorated. Kings were also priests who talked to their ancestors.
Over 150,000 pieces have been found. Their script, about 1250 BCE and later, is clearly an early form of Chinese. Many characters are still recognisable today.

In 1976 archaeologists found the untouched tomb of Fu Hao, a wife of King Wu Ding. It held bronze weapons, jade and hundreds of bronzes.

Oracle bones name her as a general who led thousands of soldiers. Women of this era could be powerful, though this was not the case later.

About 1046 BCE, the Zhou people, from the west, defeated the last Shang king at the battle of Muye. The date is debated; various scholars say 1045 to 1027 BCE.

The Zhou needed to explain why they could overthrow a king. They invented a political idea that would last 3,000 years.
This is the Mandate of Heaven (tianming). It gave rulers authority but also a warning: rule badly and you can be overthrown. Chinese emperors used it for the next 3,000 years.

Some historians suspect the Mandate was made up after the fact to justify the Zhou conquest. Others think it was sincere.

Also, a famous story says a scholar, Wang Yirong, discovered oracle bones in 1899 when he saw 'dragon bones' in a pharmacy. Historians doubt parts of that tale. What is solid: the bones were being ground into medicine and the finds revealed Shang writing.

The Rigveda age

The Rigveda was composed in the Punjab, probably between 1500 and 1000 BCE, the same centuries as Shang China's oracle bones. It had no writing, only memory. Priests learned thousands of verses by ear with great exactness.

Its hymns praise Indra, Agni and Soma, and its river names include the Sindhu and the Sarasvati. One famous hymn describes the Battle of the Ten Kings on the Parushni, usually identified as the Ravi.

After about 1000 BCE, iron and Painted Grey Ware mark a move east into the Ganga-Yamuna doab. Shang bronze chariots and Vedic war chariots both owe something to the same steppe tradition.

Five things to remember

  1. The Shang (c. 1600-1046 BCE) used oracle bones.
  2. Oracle bone script is the earliest Chinese writing.
  3. Fu Hao was a queen and general.
  4. The Zhou defeated the Shang around 1046 BCE.
  5. The Mandate of Heaven said bad rulers can lose the right to rule.

Think about it

  • Is the Mandate of Heaven a good way to keep a ruler honest?
  • Which is more powerful, writing or memory? Why?
